newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ZWACK DOWNPLAYS GOVERNMENT OPTIMISM ON '97.
newsitem.headline: ZWACK DOWNPLAYS GOVERNMENT OPTIMISM ON '97.

text.p: Hungary's spirits producer Zwack Unicum Rt said on Wednesday it did not share the government's optimism of a recovery in consumption and was therefore conservative in its plans for 1997.

"In contrast with the government's positive forecast on consumption recovery, our company is more conservative in assessing the market," Zwack's CEO Imre Sivo told a news conference after Zwack's annual general meeting.
"On the spirits market we do not see a real recovery," he said. "Instead, we see consumption shifts towards cheap products due to a fall in demand," Sivo added.

The group, which is engaged primarily in the production of brand-name alcoholic beverages, planned to increase its IAS group pre-tax profit to 692 million forints on sales of 15.62 billion in 1997, although in lower sales volumes.
"The first quarter justified these expectations," Sivo said, adding that the company was profitable amid lower turnover due to strict cost control.

For the January-March period Zwack reported a two percent rise in IAS group pre-tax profit to 87 million forints, while its gross sales fell to 2.821 billion forints from 2.965 billion forints in the same period of 1996.
Zwack, hard hit by the black market in Hungary, had a pre-tax profit of 579 million forints on sales of 14.231 billion in 1996.

On investments, Sivo said Zwack planned to spend 330 million forints on a management information system, renewal of the company's fleet of company cars and production, while this year's plans do not include the launch of new investment projects.

Sivo said the company completed a 500 million forint plus investment in Kecskemet, in central Hungary, where it has established what it claims is central Europe's most modern fruit spirits distillery.
The company will spend 300 million forints on a 15 percent dividend payout on the 1996 earnings, the same as a year earlier. Dividend payments will start on June 23.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Zwack shares closed at 4,000 forints, up five.
